How quickly can a founder make a comeback? Jensen Huang did it in just 11 days, setting a remarkable pace by corporate standards.

Steve Jobs took 12 years to return to Apple. Larry Page needed 10 years to return to Google, Howard Schultz 8 to return to Starbucks, Jack Dorsey 7 to return to Twitter, and Michael Dell 3 to return to Dell.

Huang’s timeline was considerably brisker:
Nov 12: He resigned as CEO.
Nov 17: The board said it “does not intend to reinstate” him.
Nov 23: That same board voted unanimously to bring him back.

After the reinstatement, $NVDA rose 26% premarket, adding roughly $790B. The US stock market gained $3T in market cap.

Turns out founders can be surprisingly hard to replace.
